title: Computer/mouse use >4 h/day and CANS
study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohorts
population: Regular computer-using workers; prospective cohorts, follow-up ≥1 year
office_applicability: Direct for computer-worker CANS; not specific for CTS or isolated neck pain
notes: Use as a broad computer-related neck/upper-limb exposure flag, not as a CTS coefficient.

title: Self-reported workplace sitting and low-back pain
population: Occupational and non-occupational populations; 79 studies overall
office_applicability: Partially direct; occupational pooled estimate is mainly cross-sectional
temporal_design: Predominantly cross-sectional for this pooled estimate
notes: The pooled estimate does not validate a universal ≥6 h/day causal threshold.

title: Workplace sitting and neck/shoulder pain
population: Occupational and non-occupational populations; occupational subgroup
office_applicability: Partially direct; pooled occupational association is mainly cross-sectional
temporal_design: Predominantly cross-sectional for this pooled estimate
notes: Association only; should not be converted into an individual disease probability.

title: Prolonged sitting and low-back pain
population: Adults; 49 observational studies in review, 27 cross-sectional/survey studies in meta-analysis
office_applicability: Partially direct; office-worker subgroup effect was smaller
notes: Supports sedentary exposure as a modifiable context, not a validated disease threshold.

title: Prospective risk factors for non-specific neck pain in office workers
study_type: Systematic review of prospective office-worker evidence
population: Office workers; 20 papers from 10 prospective cohorts plus 2 RCTs
office_applicability: Direct
notes: Reported associations included low workplace satisfaction RR 1.28, low task variation RR 1.27, and a keyboard-position finding RR 1.46; many other factors were limited/conflicting.

title: High repetition and clinically assessed CTS
population: 17 occupational cohorts; 1,051,707 workers and 9,270 CTS cases; mainly US and European workers
office_applicability: Indirect for ordinary desk work unless true high-repetition exposure is present
source_label: Hassan et al. 2022 · prospective CTS review
notes: I² 31%. Measure actual mechanical exposure rather than substituting generic computer hours.

title: Force intensity and clinically assessed CTS
population: Occupational cohorts; clinically assessed CTS
office_applicability: Indirect for ordinary desk work; relevant only if meaningful force exposure exists
source_label: Hassan et al. 2022 · prospective CTS review
notes: I² 0%.

title: High ACGIH Hand Activity Level and CTS
population: Occupational cohorts; clinically assessed CTS
office_applicability: Indirect unless task exposure matches high HAL
source_label: Hassan et al. 2022 · prospective CTS review
notes: I² 0%.

title: High Strain Index and CTS
population: Occupational cohorts; clinically assessed CTS
office_applicability: Indirect unless task is appropriate for Strain Index assessment
source_label: Hassan et al. 2022 · prospective CTS review

title: Strain Index >5.1 and lateral epicondylitis
population: 5 prospective studies; 5,036 workers and 318 clinically assessed LE cases
office_applicability: Indirect unless task exposure is appropriate for Strain Index
notes: More defensible than using generic mouse-hours as an LE predictor.

title: Forearm rotation exposure and lateral epicondylitis
population: 5 prospective studies; 5,036 workers and 318 clinically assessed LE cases
office_applicability: Indirect; only if substantial forearm-rotation exposure is actually present
notes: The review reported relevant forearm rotation exposure definitions such as >4 h/day or ≥45° for a large proportion of work time.

title: Non-neutral posture and chronic low-back pain
population: Occupational cohort and case-control studies; mixed occupations
office_applicability: Indirect; mostly not office-specific
notes: Do not convert a single observed angle into this OR; exposure duration and task context differ.

title: Arm elevation and specific shoulder disorders
study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of occupational studies
population: European occupational cohorts/case-control studies; mainly manual/mixed work
office_applicability: Indirect for typical office work
source_label: van der Molen et al. · occupational shoulder review
notes: Use only when genuine arm-elevation exposure exists; do not infer rotator-cuff disease from age/BMI alone.

title: Overweight and carpal tunnel syndrome
population: 1,379,372 individuals; mainly Western/European general populations
office_applicability: Indirect/general susceptibility factor
notes: A susceptibility association, not an office ergonomic exposure.

title: Obesity and carpal tunnel syndrome
population: 1,379,372 individuals; mainly Western/European general populations
office_applicability: Indirect/general susceptibility factor
notes: A susceptibility association, not an office ergonomic exposure.

title: Arm support plus alternative mouse for neck/shoulder disorders
population: 15 RCTs, 2,165 office workers overall
certainty: Moderate for selected comparison; overall evidence limitations
office_applicability: Direct
notes: Specific combination; do not generalize to all ergonomic equipment.

title: Active breaks / postural change in office workers
study_type: Systematic review of controlled office-worker trials
population: 8 RCTs + 3 non-randomized office-worker trials
certainty: Moderate for active breaks/postural change and no productivity harm
office_applicability: Direct
notes: Evidence does not establish one universal magic break interval.

title: Physical activity plus ergonomics and back-pain intensity
study_type: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of office-worker RCTs
population: 24 RCT/cluster-RCTs, 7,080 office workers; follow-up ≥24 weeks
office_applicability: Direct
notes: Suggests modest benefit for multicomponent approaches; most comparisons were null/minor.

title: Workplace micro-exercise for neck/shoulder pain
population: 19 RCTs, 2,732 sedentary workers
certainty: Moderate GRADE for combined neck/shoulder pain
office_applicability: High; sedentary-worker population, though not exclusively office workers
notes: Neck disability g −0.45 (−0.73 to −0.17); isolated neck-pain estimate was highly heterogeneous (I² 98%).

title: Sleep problems and subsequent chronic musculoskeletal pain
study_type: Systematic review/meta-analysis of prospective adult cohorts
population: 16 articles from 11 populations; 116,746 adults; not office-specific
office_applicability: Indirect contextual/prognostic evidence
notes: Bidirectional relationship. Does not validate a −1 protective score for 7–9 h sleep.

title: Office-chair interventions and musculoskeletal outcomes
population: 2 RCTs, 10 repeated-measures studies and 2 prospective cohorts
office_applicability: Direct/mostly seated-work context
notes: Chair fit remains an ergonomic engineering issue, but chair replacement alone is not a validated pain-prevention treatment.
